title: Sustainable farming practices

match.reason: No bank point teaches sustainable farming practices that protect soil and water over time; the closest, Farming innovations, covers crop rotation and stubble mulching only as ways to work around limits, and it does not cover no-till, tree planting, rotational grazing or the idea of keeping land productive for the long term.

draft.title: Sustainable farming practices
card: seeds are sown without ploughing, so the soil is left covered by old crop stalks. This helps hold soil in place and keeps moisture in.
different crops are grown in turn on the same paddock. This stops one crop using up the same nutrients every year.
trees and shrubs on a farm have roots that bind soil and slow wind and water. Their shade and shelter also help stock and crops.
stock are moved between paddocks so each one gets time to recover. Grass keeps its cover, so the soil is less likely to wash or blow away.
draft.remember: Sustainable practices protect the soil and water that the farm depends on, so it can keep producing.

a.q: A farmer moves her sheep between paddocks every few weeks so the grass can regrow. Which practice is this?
a.why: Moving stock between paddocks so each can recover is rotational grazing. It is not crop rotation, which changes the crops grown in a paddock, not where animals graze.
a.clue: Think about what is being moved from paddock to paddock.

b.q: Dan grows wheat near Horsham. Each year he sows without ploughing, leaving old stalks on the soil. Why does this help the land stay productive?
opts: Stalks cover the soil, so less is lost and moisture stays
Stalks add a different crop, so nutrients are not used up
Stalks give the paddock time to recover from grazing
Stalks bind the soil with roots, so wind is slowed
b.why: In no-till farming the soil is not ploughed and stays covered by stalks, which protects it and keeps moisture in. Growing a different crop in turn is crop rotation, and Dan is not doing that here.
b.clue: Focus on what is left on the soil surface and what it does.

b.best: Stalks cover the soil, so less is lost and moisture stays
